item.title: SCP-166: -1
item.content:encoded: I just checked to see SCP-166. Everything is different; it was re-written. Changed by vote; old SCP-166 was is better.

A few things. One is the copious amount of red, its a bit jarring and seems very unnecessary so I would cut that if I were you. Two, this thing isn't Apollyon. It is inevitable yes, but its not going to end the world, and its effects can be easily contained by supressing AI research into the field of music and not letting people listen. Also I feel that there has to be a better reason for it to be an "anomaly," constants in AI happen all of the time and I don't see why this one is any different. I also don't see why the SCP number is censored, as as far as I could tell the article had no mention of the need to censor that. That ties in to another issue I had, with the Department of Miscommunications. That feels just tacked on, and it serves no narrative purpose. Right now I am downvoting, but this thing has potential I think.

item.title: SCP-5445:
item.content:encoded: I've been mulling over the lack of "articles that involve non-Western cultures where the focus of the article isn't 'behold, it's [thing, either perceived or real that is particular to the specific non-Western culture], but now it's anomalous and also sarkic" and this fits the bill (heh) quite nicely. Not a million percent onboard with everyone's favorite imperialist sea snail being involved, but screw it - it's a punchy article, bizarre concept, and well-excecuted. Easy +1

item.title: Re: KTO-0001-Bellfather "Overwatch Council": +1
item.content:encoded:
This is an astonishing GOC article that flips the Foundation on-top of its head. First, the content warning: please heed it. Okay, going into the article itself: I'm blown away. This concept, just on its face, has so much potential. I love the idea behind the Foundation just being a rag-tag conglomeration of all the GoI's unilaterally hating the Coalition. "Keep your enemies closer," and all of that. I love the detail and synopsis of each of the Bellfather members. You can tell that a ton of time has been reserved for figuring out how to implement the differing characters and their involvement with the Foundation's directive. The format that it follows with the messages really helps the reader follow along with the article, with the ending being just so captivating. Seriously people, expand upon this. Characterizing the Overwatch Command like this could really lead to so much more good content. It also kinda revitalizes the "Foundation is evil" vibe that I've always digged. Good, good job author!

Forwarding my original review from the Thread onto here. Nothing else to say or critique. This is legitimately wonderful :)

item.title: Dire Wolf: Re: Author Post
item.content:encoded: ;-; Well, if you don't find the discrepancy bothersome, then my reason for pulling them off is nullified. If I wanted to take them off the hub whether you told me to or not I would've done it already, so rest assured that hearing your voice on this soothes my worries. Thanks for making such a fleshed out canon, and such fleshed out characters, for me to write in, and for me to put through AI isolation~!

My review on the Art Exchange forum:

This is some mind-bendy Department of Miscommunications shit (yay, another baby of mine that has a life of its own on this site, love seeing these things crop up — though before you think me rude let me be the first to admit that it may be my baby but I am not the only parent) about music! I critiqued this before it got sent out, and I am glad to see the changes that happened. My favorite lines are still in here (Mr. Measure, a nice middle note) but a lot of what I felt was the more generic "going crazy" stuff is gone. I really have no idea what is happening in this skip (even though I know the Misters are the three computers), but I do really like it. Fits the DoMc vibe perfectly.

My opinion hasn't changed. +1

item.title: ███-3955: best December 25th of my life
item.content:encoded:
Boy, am I ever so lucky to be blessed with this gift. I asked for something complex and puzzle-y relating to music and one of my other interests. Henzoid went above and beyond, including elements of DoMC, AI, math, surrealism, esoteric classes, and actual composed snippets. I'm still figuring this one out, and it still totally blows me away. I'm excited to declass it soon; keep your eyes out for that.

Thank you to DarkStuff and Elogee for organizing the Art Exchange and for assigning me such a talented and like-minded gifter. Thank you Henzoid for being awesome. Thank you to pinch-hitters for making sure everyone enjoys the holiday season.

Merry Christmas, Happy Holidays, Wishful Winters, Super Solstice Season, etc.

item.title: ███-3955: Happy Giftmas!
item.content:encoded:
Gravity drags me deep beneath the cavity in the rocky sand
Blue turns to pitch black as I sink into the land
Gravity renders me a ragdoll, tumbling to the chasm floor
Looking up at the ceiling miles below the shore

Licensing Stuff
Boo, did I scare ya?

All images and music made by me, Henzoid.

Huh, I guess I didn't really need a collapsible to say that, but here we are.

Thanks Licensing Team! You guys rock.

This SCP was written in honor of the lovely Placeholder McD for the Holiday Gift-Swap. This gift was super fun to write, in part because Placeholder and I have near-identical taste in SCPs. In fact, though the main premise is brand new, I've been meaning to do a music SCP like this for quite some time, but never found the motivation. But, enough about me, here's to Placeholder MCD: An incredible author, and a lovely human being. Cheers!

item.title: SCP-5365:
item.content:encoded:
I love this! It's cute, it has an edge of comedy, and it is pretty clever retake of Sigurros/239 kinda stuff but with less existential horror that ended up making it kinda too big to really care about.

Nonetheless, this article scared the shit out of me.

It reminded me how much environment shapes a child's, and even an adult's, perception of the world. I had always been particularly easy to sway as a kid, I can't count how many times I cried to my parents for snacks I saw on television and I'm sure I at least doubled their electric bills by insisting that I won't eat cold rice and forcing them to keep our rice warm 24/7. To even consider that the same "innocent" faith in honesty could shift and transform the real world, and hurts others…

+1, and not only because it's a gift.
